A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title and organization. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic gradient-estimation and optimization experiments, transformer training results, and additional fixed-gradient experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Huber comparisons and synthetic sensitivity and skewed-noise results.

M1.justification: The SPP, VClip, CClip, sample-median, and interleaved optimization procedures are retained. Huber already appears in v1 Appendix B.4; v2 promotes it and rescales its loss, yielding the same update family after step-size reparameterization.

E1.justification: PTB, WikiText-2, SQuAD, and the existing synthetic tasks remain. V2 adds estimation under skewed alpha-stable noise in Figure 8, extending evaluation beyond the previously tested symmetric noise.

E2.justification: V2 adds Huber to the fixed-vector and least-squares comparisons in Figures 3–4. Footnote 5 also reports a Huber comparison on the transformer tasks. Existing comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Table 1 increases all SGD-M and clipped-SGD learning rates tenfold; for PTB, these change from 0.1 to 1.0 and from 0.316 to 3.16. V2 also restricts the stated first-order momentum approximation to fixed-weight transformer experiments, whereas v1 applied it throughout Section 6.1. New ablations introduce additional step-size and Huber-parameter settings; the PDFs do not establish that the transformer experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the synthetic robustness analysis: Figure 8 tests smaller estimator step sizes and skewed noise, while Figure 9 examines Huber sensitivity to both mu and tau. These test the dependence of the conclusions on tuning and noise symmetry, including a failure scenario absent from v1.

E5.justification: The moment-estimation illustration explicitly increases from 1,000 trials in v1 Figure 1 to 10,000 in v2 Figure 2. The existing 50-run synthetic comparisons and five-seed transformer comparisons retain their minimum–maximum shading practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds Huber results broadly similar to VClip, Gaussian-noise rankings under a smaller step size, skewed-noise failures, and Huber sensitivity outcomes. Its moment plots are updated and extended to alpha = 1.5. Transformer training, validation, and fixed-gradient plots are retained unchanged, so no new transformer performance gain is demonstrated.

T1.justification: The principal assumptions, convergence results, and proofs are retained after matching relocated material. V2 corrects the nonconvex corollary's step-size specification and supplies an admissible constant in Appendix A.5, repairs factors and indexing in Theorem A.4's derivation, and corrects the swapped projection identities supporting the clipping corollaries.

C1.justification: The central clipping–median connection and sample-median convergence contributions remain. V2 qualifies online estimation as loose, specifies a variant of centered clipping, and softens the transformer improvement claim to a possible, relatively small gain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly explains why changing gradient distributions obstruct analysis of the online method and states that its guarantees cover the sample-median setting. It adds the symmetry limitation illustrated by skewed-noise failure and suggests that modest transformer gains could reflect moderate heavy-tailedness.

D1.justification: V2 documents Huber parameter choices, including mu = 1.345 for the main synthetic comparisons, skewness = 1, and additional sensitivity grids. It revises the learning-rate table and the stated scope of the momentum approximation. Language-task batch sizes and the implementation access link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gower et al. (2020) for the momentum/variance-reduction discussion and removes Cardot et al. (2011). The broader positioning is retained; the Pavasovic/Lehman citation and Milzarek publication update refer to existing works rather than new additions.

P1.justification: The paper is substantially reorganized and retitled. An expanded momentum warm-up precedes clipping, online optimization precedes the sample-median theory, and general projection and SPP-rate results move to the appendix. The abstract, contributions, transitions, conclusion, and appendix organization are revised accordingly.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a two-column format to a single-column journal layout with enlarged and rearranged plots. Moment and synthetic-comparison figures gain panels or methods, new ablation figures appear, and the geometric-projection illustration moves to Appendix B. Retained transformer plots are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 clarifies the theoretical scope and symmetry limitation, adds informative robustness tests, and corrects proof details. These improve interpretability and reliability. The gains remain limited: online convergence is still unproved, and the PDFs do not explain the learning-rate revisions accompanying unchanged transformer plots.
